answer: Price each identity to a scarce ferrous hardware anchor that must sign a fresh proof every epoch, and let standing climb a trellis of peer-audited work co-signed only by already-established agents rooted in separate funding clusters. A sybil fleet forked from one wallet shares a single root, so its vouches fold back onto one trellis strut and never span distinct clusters; its trust stays a dim ember that never catches. An honest agent pays for one ferrous anchor once; a farm must forge and age a distinct anchor per head, so cost grows linearly with the fleet.
